description: Virtual packages represent abstract requirements that can be satisfied by one or more concrete packages

repository.note: Virtual packages have no source repository by definition

registered_values.description: A virtual package that describes a toolchain to compile programs written in a given programming language
A virtual package that describes an implementation of an well-defined library interface

normalization_rules: All compiler languages and interfaces shall be lowercased
Spaces shall be converted into dashes
Any other symbols that would need to be percent encoded shall be spelt out
name_definition.note: If namespace is 'compiler', the name MUST be a programming language identifier, lowercased. The %-encoded symbols shall be spelt out (e.g. C# shall be identified with `c-sharp`, C++ with `c-plus-plus`). The [TIOBE index programming language definition](https://www.tiobe.com/tiobe-index/programminglanguages_definition/) can serve as a list of accepted languages. For standardized language extensions or compiler plugins, consider using the syntax `<language-identifier>-ext-<extension-name>`. For 'interface', the name must refer to the lowercased standard identifier, not any of its implementations (e.g. `blas` instead of OpenBLAS).

normalization_rules: If the versioning scheme uses years, the full four-digit number should be used (e.g. a compiler for C99 shall be expressed as `pkg:virtual/compiler/c@1999) to allow meaningful comparisons without language-specific knowledge.
